primary_claim_rechecks.result: Pinned config supports 93 text layers, 69 KDA and 24 explicitly listed MLA layers, 896 routed experts/16 selected, two shared experts and vocabulary 163840. Native compressed-tensors metadata uses MXFP4 groups of 32 with null input/output activation quantization and non-expert exclusions. Publisher 2.8T/104B and MXFP8 training headlines are preserved as claims; no all-module runtime activation inference is made.

primary_claim_rechecks.topic: Kimi NVIDIA precision and patched vLLM
primary_claim_rechecks.result: Mixed configuration has NVFP4 expert weight/activation groups of 16 and FP8_PB_WO attention entries. Card documents approximately 1.6 TB download and an 8-B300 patched vLLM route with runtime_patches/sitecustomize.py and mutable kimi-k3 image. Three replacement PRs remain open. Blocking the generic atlas vLLM NVFP4 profile while documenting the separate publisher patch route is justified; it is not a blanket vLLM incompatibility claim.

PR35077 merged 2026-08-19 at 5f128395910dafb98c34083dc26cb790c7674d34. Official compare API reports v0.5.21 ahead by 2211 and behind by zero. The PR author reports 197/200 GSM8K on eight GB300 GPUs and no speed measurement. Cookbook still prescribes a mutable NVFP4 development image; source ancestry alone is not installed-image validation.

Kimi cookbook B300 speed cells cite v0.5.18 at 71de97b2, input/output 8192/1024 and SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=4.5 for DSpark. Separate draft cards publish dataset acceptance claims with different sampling/aggregation; these do not turn the simulated speed rows into natural acceptance measurements. Inferact peak claim pairs 4 GB300 with TP16 ambiguously, correctly excluded from engine ranking.

primary_claim_rechecks.topic: Distinct drafts and Kimi DSpark implementation
primary_claim_rechecks.result: Inferact is five-layer dense MLA with feature IDs [2,23,47,71,89]; RadixArk is five-layer GQA with 64 query/16 KV heads and IDs [7,23,51,67,83]. Token/rotary layouts differ. Pinned vLLM source shares target embedding/head, projects target context, has Markov/confidence heads, fused reductions and non_causal_multi_token_decode=True inside draft attention. The original target-verification wording was corrected.

Recomputed 69*96*128*128*4 = 434110464 bytes = 414 MiB for the stated FP32 matrix-state thought experiment. This excludes convolutions, snapshots, padding and runtime sharding. Cookbook pool ratio divides target MLA token cache by DCP while retaining replicated draft cache, with scheduler-specific ordinary and speculative slots. The atlas correctly avoids dividing every memory component by DCP8.

primary_claim_rechecks.topic: DeepSeek 43 target layers and three draft stages
primary_claim_rechecks.result: Root num_hidden_layers=43 and num_nextn_predict_layers=1 coexist with reference n_mtp_layers=3. Reference constructor creates 43 target Blocks and three DSparkBlocks, the latter at indices43-45. Full 46-element compression schedule is 43 target entries beginning [0,0] then alternating 4/128 and ending4, plus three trailing zeroes. Enumerated target loop confirms feature IDs40/41/42 are zero-based.

Root FP8/e4m3/ue8m0/block128 metadata does not erase expert_dtype=fp4. Reference source stores paired FP4 values in float4_e2m1fn_x2 and E8M0 scales per32 expert values, while FP8 weights have 128-sized blocks. Generic all-FP8 or NVIDIA-NVFP4 labels are correctly avoided.

primary_claim_rechecks.topic: Exact DeepSeek 0731 engine support and counts
primary_claim_rechecks.result: Exact publisher card supplies both engines. Current vLLM recipe has TP1/DP4+EP and probabilistic seven-proposal DSpark; card example is greedy. SGLang documents bundled DSpark without a separate drafter, default five proposals/six verification tokens and upstream TP4 on four GB300 GPUs/v0.5.16. Local eight-GPU adaptations remain unmeasured. Preview-family284B/13B versus SGLang exact0731 table304/13B remains an explicitly unresolved main-plus-draft accounting question; exact catalog counts are null.

Publisher supplies Python message encoders/parsers rather than Jinja; engine-specific parser names are retained. Publisher recommends permitting up to384K output tokens for high/max effort. Local64K caps are explicitly a shorter experiment and cannot satisfy that output budget.

Kimi base has custom Kimi K3 terms; NVIDIA checked-in file is byte-identical while its card separately names NVIDIA Open Model Agreement. DeepSeek pinned MIT file and card expressly cover the repository and weights. This confirms stated artifact metadata, not a legal compliance determination.
